solutions.check: clues read from the FT's printable PDF (PDF has no vector grid), the grid backsolved from their numbering, the one grid that fits; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Used feature on a watch

definitions.meaning: not new, previously owned by someone else
the thin pointer that sweeps round the dial marking off each sixty-count

explanation.definitionFit: Pre-owned goods are sold this way, and the same phrase names the fastest-moving pointer on a timepiece dial.

clue.text: Boycott initially bowls in game — or bats?

indicators.note: in says the first letter of bowls is placed inside the shuffled letters
bats, meaning crazy, says the letters of game and or are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks out just the opening letter of the word bowls

explanation.surface: A cricket question: did Geoffrey Boycott start by bowling, or was he a batsman?
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott was a famous English cricket batsman, which makes 'bowls' and 'bats' look like cricket. 'bats' scrambles GAMEOR into EMARGO, and 'in' puts B, the first letter of bowls ('initially'), inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ban on trade with a country is a form of official refusal to deal with it.

clue.text: Letter's nothing great

parts.note: nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O
mega is slang for great or excellent

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone's letter is nothing special.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the final character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Father almost is furious about king's unenlightened period

indicators.note: almost says the word for father loses its final letter

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father

indicators.note: about says the rage word goes round the letter for king

parts.note: rages means is furious
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A father nearly losing his temper over a king's backward times.
explanation.definitionFit: The early medieval centuries in Europe are traditionally seen as a time of little learning.

clue.text: Right off the bat when bowler's let go?

definitions.meaning: a bowler is a hard round hat, so this is the moment that hat falls

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means instantly, from the old signal of a dropped hat starting a race, and a bowler is a kind of hat.

clue.text: Cutting from inside, a dentist makes one numb

indicators.note: Cutting from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something a dentist uses inside the mouth makes the patient numb.
explanation.definitionFit: To dull sensation is to remove feeling, as an anaesthetic does.

clue.text: Pop's certainly in church

indicators.note: in says the word for certainly goes inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OK means certainly or all right

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether fizzy pop is definitely allowed in church.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a brand of fizzy soft drink, and pop is a general term for such drinks.

clue.text: Cold, it later fluctuates with temperature dropping in here?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: dropping in says the temperature letter is put inside the shuffled letters
fluctuates says the letters of it later shift around

explanation.surface: A weather report: cold now, warmer later, with temperatures falling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluctuates' turns ITLATER into ATLITER, and 'dropping in' puts T inside it. The definition leans on 'dropping in' too: a cat makes its droppings in here.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray of absorbent material is where a pet does its business indoors.

clue.text: Studious person turned up who developed specialised skill

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue says the swot word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a wonk is a studious or overly bookish person

indicators.note: developed says the letters of who are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A bookish student turned up and developed an expert skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical expertise is knowledge of how to get something done.

clue.text: Source of music from stereo booming on the way back?

indicators.note: on the way back says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Music blaring from a car stereo on the journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes EOBO out of 'stereo booming' and 'on the way back' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind instrument produces musical sound.

clue.text: Response surrounding Turkey's withdrawal

indicators.note: surrounding says the response word goes round the Turkey letters

parts.note: a reaction is a response
TR is the international code for Turkey

explanation.surface: A response to Turkey pulling out of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking back a statement is a formal pulling-back from it.

clue.text: A rear admiral traps reckless group of ships

indicators.note: traps says the naval officer letters hold the word for reckless

parts.note: mad can mean wild or reckless

explanation.surface: A rear admiral catching a careless fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleet of warships, famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Vision I put on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio says what follows is heard, not read

parts.note: I plus site (to put or place) is said the same way

explanation.surface: Someone describing a vision they broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the radio' signals sound: 'I site', with site meaning put or position, is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The ability to see is one's power of sight.

clue.text: Boss's wealth held by agent

indicators.note: held by says the riches word sits inside the agent word

parts.note: a doer is one who acts, an agent
a mine is a rich source, a wealth of something

explanation.surface: The boss's fortune is managed by an agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is a verb here, with the 's standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lord it over others is to order them about.

clue.text: I leave guy to reform group of universities

indicators.note: reform says the letters of I leave guy are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone abandoning a man to try to change him.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight elite private colleges in the north-east USA form this sporting association.

clue.text: Alien not eating women, eg Ripley

indicators.note: eating says the jumbled word takes the women letter inside
Alien means strange or foreign, so the letters of not are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ellen Ripley, heroine of the film Alien, not being eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripley is the hero of the film 'Alien', but here 'Alien' scrambles NOT into TON and Ripley is a place: towns in Derbyshire, Surrey and Yorkshire bear the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripley is an English market settlement, an example of a modest urban place.

clue.text: In Britain we picked up alcohol

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue says the letters of we are read upwards

explanation.surface: We collected alcohol in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' wants to be a homophone, but in a down clue it turns WE upwards into EW.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer or wine made in your own kitchen is a type of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Clock types broken — losing time

indicators.note: broken says the letters of types are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clock repair note: the types are broken and it loses time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes T from TYPES, and 'broken' rearranges the remaining YPES. 'Clock' is the slang verb for notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To clock someone is slang for to catch sight of them.

clue.text: Lies initially spread by politicians

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of spread

parts.note: Tories are members of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Falsehoods first circulated by politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: TORIES are members of the UK's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales told to deceive, as in a child making things up.

clue.text: Increase for a period

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a tract can be a stretch of time

explanation.surface: Raising something for a set time.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw out or lengthen something in time is to extend it.

clue.text: Fast runner — he's caught by awful cheat

indicators.note: caught by says he sits inside the jumbled letters
awful says the letters of cheat are badly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the 's being no letter

explanation.surface: A fast athlete is caught out by a dreadful cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast runner' suggests an athlete, but it is the animal. 'awful' rearranges CHEAT into CETAH before 'caught by' does its work.
explanation.definitionFit: This big cat is the quickest land animal.

clue.text: Work up into strange concoction

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the work abbreviation is read upwards

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work

indicators.note: strange says the letters of into are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stirring something into a weird brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns OP into PO; 'strange' turns INTO into TION.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed drink with supposed magical or medicinal powers is a brew.

clue.text: Fellow with no other

indicators.note: other says the letters are made otherwise, so fellow and no are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man with nobody else around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' is the anagram signal: FELLOW plus NO, rearranged. The whole clue also defines the answer, a man with no companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner who keeps to himself and has no companions.

clue.text: Nothing caught in river with last bit of bait — something that's guided to its target

definitions.text: something that's guided to its target

indicators.note: in says the nothing and caught letters go inside the river name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: last bit of picks out the final letter of bait

explanation.surface: An angler on a river catches nothing on the last of the bait.
explanation.walkthrough: The EXE is a river in Devon. 'in' puts OC inside it, and 'last bit of' adds T.
explanation.definitionFit: A French anti-ship weapon, it is a homing missile.

clue.text: Maria now returning somewhat put out

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Maria is now returning, rather put out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes RIANO out of 'Maria now' and 'returning' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Being broadcast means a programme is transmitted to listeners.

clue.text: Fresh ink I spilled penning government's flyer

indicators.note: penning says the government letter is enclosed by the jumbled letters
spilled says the letters of fresh ink I are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: Someone spilled fresh ink while writing a government bird leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'spilled' scrambles it with INK I, and 'penning' places G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly coloured fish-eating bird darts low over rivers.

clue.text: Not in favour of very old things? No question

indicators.note: No says the question abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: antiques are very old collectable things
ques is an abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes very old things, and will take no questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposed to something; against it.

clue.text: Small bit of land that is surrounded?

definitions.text: Small bit of land that is surrounded?

indicators.note: surrounded says the that-is letters go round the other two

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: bit of picks out the opening letter of land

explanation.surface: A tiny piece of ground enclosed on all sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded' puts S and L ('bit of' land) inside IE. The whole clue also defines: land encircled by water.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island is a piece of ground with water all round.

clue.text: Big laddie's last toy thrown out

indicators.note: out says the letters are thrown into a new order
last picks out the final letter of laddie

explanation.surface: A big boy's newest toy is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'out' scrambles it with TOY and E ('last' of laddie's).
explanation.definitionFit: Important or remarkable enough to deserve attention.
